items.stem: An inbox rule in Outlook is best described as:

options.text: Conditions that, when met, trigger actions on arriving mail, with optional exceptions
options.rationale: Correct: rules evaluate conditions, run actions and respect exceptions.

options.text: A way to permanently delete the mailbox
options.rationale: Rules organise mail; they do not delete mailboxes.
Rules act on messages, not calendars.

options.text: A read-only report of mail volume
options.rationale: Rules act on mail; they are not a report.

items.explanation: Correct: an inbox rule is a set of conditions that trigger actions on arriving mail, with optional exceptions.

items.stem: Which TWO statements about Outlook email organisation are correct? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Focused Inbox separates likely-important mail onto a Focused tab
options.rationale: Correct: Focused Inbox splits Focused and Other.

options.text: A Quick Step can apply several actions to a message in one click
options.rationale: Correct: Quick Steps bundle multiple actions.

options.text: Rules can only ever move mail to the Deleted Items folder
options.rationale: Rules can perform many actions, not just delete.

options.text: Focused Inbox encrypts messages end to end
options.rationale: Focused Inbox sorts mail; it is not an encryption feature.

items.explanation: Correct: Focused Inbox sorts mail onto Focused/Other and a Quick Step bundles several actions.

items.stem: You flag an email in Outlook. What is one standard consequence across Microsoft 365?

options.text: It appears as a task in Microsoft To Do
options.rationale: Correct: flagged Outlook mail syncs into Microsoft To Do.
Flagging does not delete the message.

options.text: It becomes visible to everyone in the organisation
options.rationale: Flagging is personal; it does not share the mail.

options.text: It is converted into a calendar event automatically
options.rationale: Flagging creates a task, not a calendar event.

items.explanation: Correct: flagging an email in Outlook surfaces it as a task in Microsoft To Do.
